sources.title: Governor biography
sources.findings: Governor since 9 November 2014; third term 9 November 2024–8 November 2029; deputy from 16 May 2011; IMFC chair 18 January 2018–17 January 2021; BCom UNISA and MSc SOAS.
sources.caution: 2029 is a future scheduled term end, not completed service. Older governance page calls IMFC chair current; reject that outdated description. Other external committee roles not independently refreshed.

sources.title: Lesetja Kganyago biography
sources.findings: Birth 7 October 1965; UNISA commerce degree 1991, SOAS masters 1994; earlier Wits study incomplete.
sources.caution: Treasury deputy director-general 2004–2011 conflicts with contemporaneous government statement; use Director-General. Birthplace differs across sources; omit birthplace.

sources.title: Lesetja Kganyago profile
sources.findings: Public profile header confirms birth 7 October 1965.
sources.caution: Only public header and excerpts read, not subscriber articles. Boyne birthplace conflicts with SAHO Alexandra and raw evidence Alexandria; no birthplace claim.

sources.title: 25 March 2011 appointment statement
sources.findings: Treasury Director-General since February 2004; deputy governor effective 16 May 2011; Treasury entry 1996 and earlier SARB service 1994–1996.
sources.caution: Announcement date 25 March differs from effective date 16 May. Government praise is not independent performance assessment.

sources.title: IMFC selects Kganyago as chairman
sources.findings: Three-year IMFC chair appointment effective 18 January 2018; committee advises IMF Board of Governors.
sources.caution: Not IMF Managing Director; 2018 external roles not assumed current in 2026.

sources.title: The Chancellor
sources.findings: Elected 24 January 2025, installed 20 June 2025 as 16th Chancellor; ceremonial role; earned BCom/MSc distinct honorary DCom.
sources.caution: Chancellor does not imply executive Rector and Vice-Chancellor; honorary doctorates are not earned research degrees.

sources.title: Installation of the 16th Chancellor
sources.findings: 23 June 2025 report describes preceding Friday installation and inaugural address.
sources.caution: Report date is not installation date; cross-check official chancellor page for 20 June.

sources.title: 20 October 2026 payments conference address
sources.findings: Discusses non-bank access, PayShap, interoperable QR codes and payment identity; closing outlines future implementation milestones.
sources.caution: Read opening pages and closing milestones, not every middle paragraph or linked research. November 2026 framework and 2027 pilots are plans, not completed rollouts.

sources.title: 29 October 2026 low-growth address
sources.findings: Argues price stability supports growth but cannot replace structural reform; describes 3% inflation target adopted November 2025 with one-percentage-point tolerance.
sources.caution: Read speech body; economic diagnoses and projections attributed to speaker, not independently proven outcomes or investment advice. Do not turn inflation target into interest rate.

sources.title: 12 November 2026 acceptance speech
sources.findings: Dated address at Sunday Times awards in Johannesburg discusses trust, transparency, accountability and independent institutions.
sources.caution: Official written speech supports recent activity; no video witnessed or precise award category independently established. Private family details omitted.
